partB.q: Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an agreement enforceable by law is a:
A stipulation essential to the main purpose of a contract of sale is called a:
An agreement made with a minor is:

partA.question: Ram agrees to sell his car to Shyam for ₹5 lakh. Both are adults of sound mind, both freely agree, and the purpose is lawful. Is this a valid contract? State the essentials of a valid contract.

scheme.step: Provision: Sec 2(h) definition + Sec 10 (essentials of valid contract)
scheme.model: Sec 2(h): an agreement enforceable by law is a contract. Sec 10: agreements made by free consent of competent parties, for lawful consideration and lawful object, not expressly declared void.

scheme.step: Essentials listed (offer & acceptance, intention, consideration, capacity, free consent, lawful object, not void)
scheme.model: Lawful offer and acceptance, intention to create legal relations, lawful consideration, capacity of parties, free consent, lawful object, certainty, possibility of performance, not declared void.

scheme.step: Applied to the facts + conclusion: valid contract
scheme.model: All essentials are satisfied in the facts, so it is a valid contract enforceable by law.

partA.question: Distinguish between a condition and a warranty under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930. What remedy does the buyer have in each case?

scheme.model: Condition: stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract. Warranty: stipulation collateral to the main purpose.

scheme.step: Differences (nature, effect of breach, possible treatment of condition as warranty)
scheme.model: Breach of condition gives a right to repudiate; breach of warranty gives only damages. A breach of condition may be treated as a breach of warranty (Sec 13), not vice versa.

scheme.step: Remedies: repudiate + damages for condition; damages only for warranty
